newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan envoy to meet Cambodian premiers.
newsitem.headline: Japan envoy to meet Cambodian premiers.

text.p: Japan's special envoy to Cambodia, Yukio Imagawa, said he will meet with the two Cambodian premiers individually next week to urge them not to endanger the fragile coalition, Japanese media reported on Sunday.
Leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations and Russia agreed on Friday to send Japanese and French envoys to Cambodia to study the situation there.

Japan, the largest aid donor to Cambodia, had expressed concern over the mounting tensions between the two premiers, Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, following the chase and capture of Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot.

"I will call on them (premiers) to protect what Cambodia has achieved with regard to the attainment of peace and the reconstruction of the country, toward which Japan has also lent its support," Imagawa told Japan's Kyodo News.

Imagawa, a former Japanese ambassador to Cambodia, said he feared the rivalry between the two leaders could endanger the fragile coalition government and may ultimately spark another civil war, Kyodo reported.
The two premiers have been engaged in bitter political infighting after forming an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.

Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party wants to strike a deal with more moderate elements in the crumbling guerrilla force, a move that Hun Sen sees as a threat to his strength in the run-up to polls next year, political analysts said.
Hun Sen has branded all contact with the Khmer Rouge as illegal and told Ranariddh last week to choose between working with him in their coalition or joining the rebels.

Imagawa said Japan was strongly committed to preserving peace in the country. "One could perhaps even go so far as to say that Japan should quit the business of diplomacy in Asia if it cannot face up to this task," he said.
